page: UpCloud GPU-32xCPU-384GB-2xL40S is a GPU-accelerated server instance designed for compute-intensive and machine learning workloads. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it features 32 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz with a shared CPU allocation. The system is equipped with 384.0 GB of system memory, providing 12.0 GB of RAM per core. Acceleration is delivered via two NVIDIA L40S GPUs based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, providing a combined 96 GB of VRAM. The instance does not include local storage, and virtualization is managed via the KVM hypervisor.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance across multiple domains. In CPU-bound tasks, the instance achieves top 10% placement in both single-core and multi-core stress-ng tests, as well as Geekbench single-core and multi-core evaluations. Memory bandwidth is strong, ranking in the top 25% for both cached small-block and uncached large-block read operations, though Passmark memory scores fall into the average range. Cryptographic and compression performance is highly competitive, with bzip3 decompression and Passmark database operations placing in the top 10%. For AI workloads, LLM inference speeds for small 135M models reach top-tier levels, while medium 7B models achieve strong performance, and large 70B models operate at average speeds.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the server offers high resource density by pairing a 32-core AMD EPYC processor with dual enterprise-grade NVIDIA L40S GPUs and a substantial 384 GB memory footprint, making it a viable alternative to larger multi-GPU nodes. The lack of local storage requires external block storage integration, which is a key architectural tradeoff. This configuration is highly suited for workloads such as large language model inference, image and text processing, ray tracing, database operations, and high-throughput web serving.

Powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor with 32 vCPUs on the x86_64 architecture, the system includes 384.0 GB of RAM and two NVIDIA Ada Lovelace L40S GPUs delivering 96 GB of total VRAM. Operating on the KVM hypervisor, the instance lacks local storage, requiring external storage solutions. Benchmark results place this server in the top 10% for single-core and multi-core CPU performance, database operations, and small-model LLM inference. It delivers strong memory bandwidth and competitive text and image processing capabilities. This configuration is optimized for workloads such as AI inference, data science, ray tracing, and high-throughput database applications.
